work_package: P3 Windows CI browser smoke cross-host fixture correction

findings.title: Use host-consistent paths in the simulated macOS resolver fixture
findings.initialEvidence: Original actual smoke test passes on POSIX os.path but fails when browser.os.path is ntpath: expected the literal POSIX Mac path while resolver returns an empty string because isfile mock rejects every mixed-separator candidate. sys.platform patching does not replace host os.path.
findings.resolution: Only test fixture changed: build mac expectation with os.path.join, matching native host path semantics, with comment explaining platform/path distinction. Existing isfile/access predicates and both Mac managed detection and Windows resolver assertions remain intact.

validation.method: Independent execution of original and fixed actual single smoke method under POSIX and ntpath path modules
validation.interpretation: Original POSIX passes; original ntpath fails; fixed POSIX and fixed ntpath pass. This is simulated path-semantics evidence, not a Windows OS execution.

validation.method: Read parent real Mac smoke execution log
validation.result: 8 tests, 21.719 seconds, OK; includes actual owned-driver/launcher cleanup paths.

validation.method: Independent diff review and git diff --check
validation.result: pass; the source edit is limited to expectation construction and comment. Product browser.py has no working-tree diff.

productAssessment: No product defect identified from this failure. Real Windows sys.platform is win32 and _managed_executable bypasses the Mac application loop and retains _windows_default_browser_executable. On real Mac, os.path is POSIX and the application candidates use normal POSIX paths. The failing combination of darwin platform and ntpath is created by the cross-host test simulation.
limitations: CI job failure was supplied by parent; this independent review did not retrieve the full Windows log or classify any other CI failure.
No real Windows test run performed; Windows registry/browser resolution and whole-candidate CI remain unverified by this review.
Local targeted execution uses isolated HOME, USERPROFILE and WCW_DATA_DIR; no real browser launched in the independent four-case comparison.
